prompts.mirror:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create a new finished 16:9 landscape chapter painting for Updraft, THE SKY MIRROR.
Reference image1 is the actual game, authoritative for this place: a perfectly flat, shallow mirror of the sky with fallen LIGHT POINTS just beneath it, a little round wooden stool, a shallow enamel soap bowl, a brass bubble hoop, and a distant timber jetty. Image2 supplies ONLY the polished luminous painting style and clean continuous surfaces of the approved chapter art. Do not copy its boat, buildings or orange-sunset composition.
Emotional aim: standing on a thin sheet of water that seems to open into an infinite sky beneath your feet. Quiet, spacious, softly impossible, a place where a child mends the sky. This is an environment painting with nobody in it.
IMPORTANT CAMERA CHANGE: view from a child's eye height, about one metre above the water, looking gently across the mirror toward a visible far horizon around 42% down the image. A human standing view, NOT aerial, NOT looking straight down, NOT a bowl-and-stool close-up product still life. The viewer must instantly understand which is the sky above and which is its enormous reflection below. The unbroken level horizon establishes that space.
The lower half is an absolutely smooth glasslike sheet of shallow water reflecting the broad sky above. Show soft lavender-blue cloud masses and a few pale peach-lit edges, mirrored geometrically in the still surface. No land, no rocks, no sand, no platform, no cloud objects resting on water. No central sun, no mountains, no floating islands. The horizon is a restrained narrow pearl-apricot seam, much quieter than a blazing sunset.
Composition with clear near/far depth:
- The closest focal point, a little below centre around 48% across and 65% down, is a tiny INTENSE WHITE-GOLD POINT OF LIGHT trapped beneath the transparent skin of water. A minute brilliant core, softly diffusing warm halo and a few fine tapered rays laid along the plane, while a faint trace of reflected lavender cloud passes over it. NO physical shape, five-point star, diamond, ball, jewel or golden object. A single very faint wide elliptical ripple helps reveal the water's thin skin. The light feels close enough to reach down toward.
- Further back, at roughly 34% across, the small simple ROUND THREE-LEGGED stool carries the shallow pale blue-grey enamel bowl. A thin round brass soap hoop with a short all-brass handle rests against it. These ordinary objects are modest in scale, about 13% of the image width as a group, with all feet visibly meeting the mirror and a precise dark reflection underneath. They anchor the distance, not dominate the frame.
- A single delicate transparent soap bubble is rising above the mirror near 60% across, predominantly against the REAL sky, gently separated from its reflection below by clear space. About 11% of frame width, nearly invisible clear centre, fine pearl/rose/blue edge, one soft highlight. A tiny point of warm light has just been caught inside it. Its reflection below is correctly positioned, subtly quieter and partially lost in the reflected cloud colour: avoid two large decorative circles touching in a figure eight.
- Two other tiny light points remain underneath the mirror further away, irregularly spaced and much dimmer than the foreground one.
- Far off to the right, a very small timber jetty and its one warm lantern, as in the game reference, provide the slightest sense of a place to leave from. Keep this incidental, fading into the distance, no boat.
The overall eye travels from the close trapped light through the small soap objects to the rising bubble and spacious horizon. Large calm regions and dimensional clouds make the space breathe. Keep every important subject between 18% and 73% down for a wide-screen crop; lower centre naturally settles into quiet lavender reflection for separate UI, never a blank panel.
Colour and style: pearly lavender, muted blue, soft blush and pale apricot, small white-gold lights; rich coloured shadows with soft volumetric light, clean gently rounded wooden objects, luminous animated-film painting like reference2. Preserve warmth without an orange wash. No photographic microtextures, generic brush-stamp noise, repeated swatches, facets, triangular or diamond patterns, canvas/paper grain, waves, typography, UI, people, animals, extra props, boats or sails.
prompts.seaDolphin:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
This is the APPROVED Updraft Open Sea chapter painting. Preserve the existing boat EXACTLY: size, position, angle, full mast and rig, red four-sided sail, round wooden hull, white bow post and brass lantern, cream rails and rope swags, thwarts, pail and coil of rope. Preserve the whole composition, blue water, broad calm swell, lighting, wake, clean painting finish and crop.
Make ONE small addition: the hint of ONE common dolphin swimming alongside the boat, sharing its course toward the lower left. Place it in the water to the LEFT of the bow, around 31–35% across and 65% down, with a comfortable clear gap between it and the boat. It is a quiet companion discovered on a second look, not a new focal subject.
Show mostly a streamlined bluish-grey body just BELOW the water, with only the graceful arc of its back and small swept-back dorsal fin briefly breaking the surface. A subtle slender dolphin beak is discernible through the blue water at the front; the rest of its form including horizontal tail flukes is softened and partly obscured by the water. Keep its anatomy convincingly dolphin-like rather than a shark fin or whale. Body length about half the visible boat hull length. Soft grey-blue back, a hint of paler flank where refracted light reaches it, harmonised with the surrounding sea. A tiny glint along its wet back and a short fine disturbance in the surface; no white splash or dramatic leap, no large wake, no cartoon face or eye contact. This is an understated passing glimpse.
Do not change or repaint anything else. Do not add a pod, extra animals, passengers, landscape, new clouds, text or UI. Preserve smooth coherent shading with no repeating swatches, grain or photoreal material noise.
